stemMd: Two ions have equal concentration gradients across a membrane, but only one crosses rapidly through a particular protein. What best explains the difference?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The protein's pore selectively accommodates one ion.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The membrane necessarily contains a hole large enough for all solutes.

options.label: C
options.textMd: All ions cross lipid bilayers at identical rates.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The slower ion cannot undergo thermal motion.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The faster ion must be a protein.

explanationMd: Channel proteins can discriminate among ions through pore geometry and chemical interactions. Equal concentration gradients alone do not guarantee equal permeability or transport rates.

distractorRationale.b: Selective transport contradicts an unrestricted hole.
distractorRationale.c: Charge and hydration make unassisted crossing difficult.
distractorRationale.d: All dissolved ions undergo thermal motion.
distractorRationale.e: Ions are not converted into proteins.
